statement: The letters ABCDE are written in a row again and again: ABCDEABCDE... Below them, starting in the same column, the digits 1234567 are written again and again. In the first 200 columns, how many columns have the letter A directly above the digit 1?

choices.misconception: I divided 200 by 35 and rounded down, missing that column 1 itself counts.
I thought A and 1 meet again every 5 + 7 = 12 columns instead of every 35.
I counted the columns that have a 1, without checking whether A is above it.
I counted the columns that have an A, without checking whether 1 is below it.

hints: When do the two rows both start over at the same time?

The letters repeat every 5 columns and the digits every 7. A sits over 1 exactly when both cycles are back at their start together, which happens at a regular interval. Find that interval, then count carefully, including column 1.
A and 1 line up in column 1 and then every 35 columns, the least common multiple of 5 and 7: columns 1, 36, 71, and so on.

solutions.reliable: A is in columns 1, 6, 11, and so on, and 1 is in columns 1, 8, 15, and so on. Both happen exactly when the column number is one more than a multiple of 5 and one more than a multiple of 7, that is, one more than a multiple of 35. Those columns are 1, 36, 71, 106, 141 and 176; the next, 211, is too far. That is 6 columns. The transferable idea: two cycles realign at the least common multiple of their lengths, and counting positions needs care at the first one.
solutions.elegant: Number the columns from 0 instead of 1. A meets 1 at columns 0, 35, 70, ..., up to 199, which is every multiple of 35 from 0 to 175: 175 / 35 + 1 = 6.

whyOnTest: Repeating-cycle questions test working with positions modulo the cycle length; two cycles realign at the least common multiple, and the start column is easy to miss.
